exclusion_reason: Implemented but red because the session and lockstep fixture (FIX-019) needs a consented, allowlisted relay peer and the WebRTC/WebSocket transport binding plus DirectPlay session semantics, none of which run in this worktree — the default instance grants no consent, so every dial is refused (deny-by-default). The ws2_32 lifecycle slice is bound generically in lib/hle.mjs over the mediated Winsock in lib/net.mjs: WSAStartup writing WSADATA and WSACleanup, WSAGetLastError, socket and closesocket over the handle table, bind and connect marshaling sockaddr_in through the consent gate, send and recv, ioctlsocket FIONBIO, and the pure htons/htonl/ntohs/ntohl and inet_addr helpers.
promotion_trigger: Promote when the session fixture holds semantics with zero off-allowlist attempt.
expected_failing_assertion: No consented, allowlisted relay peer or WebRTC/WebSocket transport is bound, so the session and lockstep fixture cannot establish a link.
active_gate_evidence: The conformance suite carries a case for every served ws2_32 export (a new served surface of 15), and a dedicated test proves WSAStartup marshals WSADATA, the socket handle table serves socket/closesocket, an offline dial is refused with WSAEACCES (deny-by-default), and htons/htonl/inet_addr are byte-exact; the existing net suite keeps the offline transport failing every send with the network-down contract. The full suite stays green.
procedure: Run the session and lockstep fixture over the mediated transport.
Assert every endpoint is on the allowlist.
Assert zero off-allowlist attempt is recorded.
